title: TNF-alpha-NF-kappaB activation through pathological alpha-Synuclein disrupts the BBB and exacerbates axonopathy.
authors: Jeon, Min-Tae; Cogill, Sinnead Anne; Kim, Kyu-Sung; Kim, Yongjin; Kim, Hyerin; Lee, Chung-Yeol; Kim, Suji; Son, Suhyeon; Kim, Jeongyeon; Lee, Jaehyeok; Park, Inyeong; Cheon, Mookyung; Kim, Do-Geun
one_liner_zh: 该文研究α-Syn通过TNF-α-NF-κB通路破坏血脑屏障并导致轴突病变，虽用GAN分析病理变化，但核心是神经炎症与BBB功能，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Dysfunction of the blood-brain barrier (BBB) is recognized as a key factor in the progression of neurodegenerative diseases (NDs), but the detailed mechanisms behind its pathogenesis and impact on neurodegeneration remain elusive. This study aimed to reveal the pathological effects of alpha-Synuclein (alpha-Syn), an aggregation protein in synucleinopathy, on BBB integrity and function and identify therapeutic targets for alpha-Syn-related vasculopathy. Using a brain endothelial cell model, we investigated the pathological effect of preformed fibril alpha-Syn (PFF) on BBB integrity, employing generative adversarial network (GAN) deep learning to analyze pathological changes. We found that PFF activates immune responses, increasing endothelial monolayer permeability via the TNF-alpha-NF-kappaB pathway. Further in vivo studies with PFF induced alpha-synucleinopathy, and a transgenic animal model (G2-3) revealed that alpha-Syn aggregation disrupts the BBB, leading to axonal degeneration that was mitigated by treatment with a non-BBB-penetrating TNF-alpha inhibitor, etanercept. These findings suggest that targeting brain endothelial TNF-alpha signaling could be a potential therapeutic approach for synucleinopathy-related NDs.
abstract_zh: 血脑屏障（BBB）功能障碍被认为是神经退行性疾病（NDs）进展的关键因素，但其发病机制及其对神经变性的具体影响仍不清楚。本研究旨在揭示α-突触核蛋白（alpha-Syn）——一种在突触核蛋白病中聚集的蛋白质——对BBB完整性和功能的病理效应，并确定alpha-Syn相关血管病变的治疗靶点。利用脑内皮细胞模型，我们研究了预形成纤维alpha-Syn（PFF）对BBB完整性的病理效应，并采用生成对抗网络（GAN）深度学习分析病理变化。我们发现PFF激活免疫反应，通过TNF-alpha-NF-kappaB通路增加内皮单层通透性。进一步的体内研究使用PFF诱导的α-突触核蛋白病，以及转基因动物模型（G2-3）显示，alpha-Syn聚集破坏BBB，导致轴突变性，而通过非BBB穿透性TNF-alpha抑制剂依那西普治疗可缓解该变性。这些发现表明，靶向脑内皮TNF-alpha信号可能是突触核蛋白病相关NDs的潜在治疗策略。
